title: Liquid AI releases small long-context encoders designed for CPUs
friendlyTitle: Small Liquid AI models can read long documents on a CPU
summary: Liquid AI has released 230M- and 350M-parameter LFM2.5 encoder models with an 8,192-token context window for classification, routing, policy checks, retrieval and token-level tasks. Its published tests show the 230M model running about 3.7 times faster than ModernBERT-base at long context on CPU.
friendlySummary: Liquid AI released two small models for sorting, searching and checking text. They can handle long inputs and run on normal CPU hardware.
whyItMatters: Many production language tasks do not need a large generative model. A compact encoder running locally can lower cost and latency for intent routing, personal-data detection or document classification while keeping text on existing hardware.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Teams may be able to do useful AI work more cheaply and keep documents on their own machines.
